title: Python strict IPv6 parser silently truncates non-canonical RH3 (HEL=3) and accepts payload-length vs actual-bytes inconsistency
description: RETRACTED-PREMISE (by worker5 during 89z7 vector construction). The original claim (python strict parser silently truncates non-canonical HEL=3 RH3 and accepts payload-length inconsistency) was an artifact of a broken test vector, not a parser bug: the first HEL=3 vector draft had HEL BYTE 0x02 at offset 41 while the ext body was 32 bytes, so python's parser correctly consumed (HEL+1)*8 = 24 bytes and treated the remaining 8 ext bytes + 12 UDP bytes as the payload (24 + 20 = 44 = declared payload_len - fully self-consistent, no truncation). The subsequent UDP-length rejection was the correct verdict for a malformed packet. After fixing the HEL byte (now corpus row rh3_noncanonical_hdr_ext_len_malformed), python rejects via the RH3 canonical-length check ((len(data)-6)%16 fires on data=30) exactly like C and Rust - no parser work needed. Residual kernel: from_bytes does not cross-check that (parsed ext bytes + payload bytes) equals the declared payload_length when ext headers are present - it derives payload as the remainder, so a packet whose HEL disagrees with the actual ext body still parses self-consistently rather than failing as malformed; every consumer re-validates downstream so impact is unproven. Close as false alarm retaining this analysis; no code change.
close_reason: False alarm - corrected analysis: python's parser was correct; the vector's HEL byte was wrong (0x02 at offset 41 vs intended 0x03), making the constructed ext self-inconsistent (HEL said 24 bytes, body was 32). The parser faithfully consumed (HEL+1)*8 = 24 bytes and derived payload as the remainder (8 leaked ext bytes + 12 UDP = 20 = 44 declared - 24 consumed): self-consistent, no truncation, no payload-length violation. The UDP-length rejection was the correct verdict for that malformed packet. After fixing the vector HEL byte (now corpus row rh3_noncanonical_hdr_ext_len_malformed in 89z7), python rejects via the intended RH3 canonical-length check with the same reason as C and Rust. The genuine outputs of this investigation are the corrected vector plus the new positive two-address fallback vector srh3_two_address_in_transit_udp_fallback, both landed in 89z7. Residual (unproven, low value): from_bytes derives payload as remainder rather than cross-checking consumed+payload == declared when ext headers are present; harmless today since every consumer re-validates.
